summary: The build tools pulled in braces 3.0.3, whose recursive compilation can overflow the stack on 12000 nested braces. Use bounded Picomatch compilation for source exclusions, catalog capture and watcher patterns, removing braces from the dependency graph.

During network restoration the puzzle allowance disappeared between the visibility and text probes. Its missing-element error aborted convergence, leaving the watcher observed as revealed instead of skipped. Treat only that optional-label disappearance as absent and continue observing the unchanged model expectations.

During a correct move’s automatic reply the board temporarily shows the opponent in check. Coaching incorrectly said the solver’s king was checked and the opponent had already replied. Give neutral reply guidance until the board settles.
Scrubbing to an earlier board retained a wrong-move diagnosis and hints belonging to the frontier. Give review guidance and replace the speech context.

Trace conformance sampled again after observing convergence and could report a transient state during queued reconnect commands. Evaluate the same observation that established convergence; pin both long reconnect histories.
An interrupted audio seek could start a later request with the same cached URL before its own seek completed. Guard asynchronous playback by request identity, including stop and disposal.
A partition healed before the heartbeat lost offline commands without notifying the room client to resynchronize. A failed send closes the transport so its durable queue is replayed after healing.

An accessor returning a fresh but equivalent observation reran the speech effect, aborted its pending audio, then refused to restart the same utterance. Track text, enabled and context as scalar memos.
Puzzle voice never started because the app TTS provider sent raw HTTP without account or device headers. Compose it with current request auth while preserving cancellation and caller headers.
A preferred checkmate with trailing source moves was accepted as a nonterminal line match; legal checkmate must end the attempt before source-line validation.
Theme-driven coaching called a completed non-mating castling line checkmate. Derive success commentary from the actual board.
Unavailable puzzle data was described as an illegal solver move. Keep unavailable data distinct from attempted moves.
A knight that could be recaptured after capture was treated as hanging. Require a legal capture and absence of legal recapture.
A supported knight fork of the king on f1 and queen on d1 was absent from coaching. Require legal moves and legal capture targets, excluding pinned attacks.
An impossible FEN with the nonmoving king already checked let the chess engine capture a king and crashed tactical analysis. Reject this position for tactical claims.
A synthesis response resolving after its request was aborted started old speech. Check cancellation before handing synthesized audio to playback.
Speech synthesis loading hid the already available observation; long messages were also clamped and their live region recreated. Keep the complete words visible in a persistent live region.

The namespace-conflict rehearsal replaced v1-app-room creation with an empty step, so Wrangler rejected the later rename of RoomServerDurableObject before upload. Keep the full creation, retention and transfer history even after resume; Cloudflare applies only steps after its committed tag. Pin the failing history against Wrangler public validation.

Syncing the namespace fix with main 59cbccb32 staged already-committed incoming specs alongside product code, so the pre-commit ownership guard rejected the merge. During a merge, enforce ownership on staged changes that differ from the incoming parent; unchanged upstream specs keep their original ownership. Mixed spec conflict resolutions still fail.

Deploy run 36989073308 stopped because gamezilla-dev already owned namespace 76e8864ea97c4d329171afb8778fb729 while the still-routed legacy room Worker owned ab56d7be4eac481e81df42eac8c99aac. Explicitly pin both IDs, retain the destination under a read-only archive class, then transfer the legacy namespace into the active room class. Unknown conflicts still fail closed and deployment verifies both IDs survive.

Check on 263be4043 failed because GitHub transfer regression assertions still expected two github_subject_prefix inputs and a ci-to-github resource move after the shared CI identity module adopted oidc_subject and moved github-to-ci. Verify the immutable subject through the caller and bound_subject input and preserve the exact state move and non-destructive retirement checks.

Report catalog setup published metadata referencing frames/alice-2.html without writing the recorded snapshot blobs. Write every report and its snapshots together for completed, passing and later-edition catalog sources.

Wrangler deleted a retired Worker successfully, then exited with authentication error 10000 while listing legacy Workers Sites KV assets. Retirement now checks the exact Worker absence through authenticated inventory rather than treating an optional cleanup failure as a failed deletion. A present Worker or unreadable inventory still fails closed.

Merging migrate-secrets-to-depot-ci-1790912980154.yml onto ci/speed-up-check-workflow triggered run 36967300871 on every push: variable import failed with Invalid token, and cleanup refused to delete the feature branch. Remove the one-time migration workflow; Check, Deploy and Health already read GitHub variables and authenticate with GitHub OIDC.

Duplicated native Depot workflows read GitHub-only variables and failed with Missing identity ID for OIDC auth; their issuer also lacked the configured cloud trust. Run the three existing GitHub workflows on Depot runners, retaining their variables and OIDC issuer.

The friends spec part 7 passed its assertions but took 627 seconds against the existing 600-second task cap. Split the same friends and spaces coverage into sixteen parts, and declare and gate every added part with a separate report cache. The time cap and every scenario and model trace remain unchanged.

Puzzle recovery trace 46 at seed 0x67932 reopened Charlie offline, then failed to hydrate the recorded result after reconnection because origin health was still waiting on its 30-second backoff. Network restoration now refreshes health for each open affected actor, waking offline boot without increasing the model's convergence budget.

After the repository transfer, GitHub issued repo:gamezilla-org@336801040/gamezilla@1165464734:pull_request, but Infisical and AWS trust policies expected name-only subjects. Declare immutable owner and repository IDs in global OpenTofu config and derive the exact subject prefix and wire it into both trust policies while retaining their branch and environment restrictions.

An identical retry of a permanently rejected mutation returned applied after the original rejection response was lost. Replay now reads the permanent stored verdict, including acknowledged rejection rows.

Technical database protocol fixtures were registered as product specs without implementation bindings, failing spec, conformance and offline model shape gates. Preserve unbound reference verification in package tests and document unimplemented adapter obligations outside product specs; the separately bound indexing maintenance specifications remain registered.

Making Apalache's array map encoding the default caused assertion failures in the outside-accounts, membership-lifecycle and note-replication models. Keep the established default settings and make the alternative encoding an explicit opt-in for supported database contract models.

Apalache's default map encoding and per-transition invariant checks exceeded the rebuild model's existing 120-second CI budget at ten steps. The database contract runners opt into SMT arrays and invariant checks after the full transition choice, preserving every invariant and the same exhaustive bound while reducing solver work. Other models retain the default encoding because arrays do not support all higher-order models.

The spec ownership gate rejected the isolated database safety contract commit because it used the required Conventional Commit docs(specs) form. Recognize that form as a spec commit while continuing to require spec changes and reject mixed implementation files.

The relocated schema-safety model registered its world and binding only from a test file. The spec runner imports tests/quint/index.ts, which was missing, leaving the existing model unbound in conformance. Extracted the registration into a binding imported by the shared entry and the model test.

On PR #107 at 2a2bda778fd0e66af2a74c7e02ecea6fb80c8956, bun check's manual dispatch cancelled the required PR Check run 36959395506, leaving the PR red despite a successful manual run. Check now observes the automatic PR run and resumes cancelled runs instead of dispatching over them.
PR and manual Check runs for the same commit overwrote each other's publication receipts, so finalization could reject a fully published report. Receipts now belong to the workflow run and attempt.
PR pushes and manual Check dispatches used different concurrency groups and queued duplicate shard fleets for the same branch. Both triggers now share the branch concurrency group.

The offline journey silently stopped waiting for shell installation after twenty seconds and cut the network while a fresh deployment was still precaching. Await the browser's service-worker readiness event instead; unsupported or inactive shells fail rather than proceeding offline.

Live journeys chose WebKit on macOS, which could not cut the network for the offline scenario. Use Chrome explicitly for the live device and its popups, with the same storage isolation and CDP network controls on every host.

Tempo returned a successful protobuf JSON trace under batches with base64 span ids, but the reader only accepted OTLP resourceSpans and silently discarded every span. Accept both document shapes and normalize protobuf ids to hex for lookup and narration.
Live journeys could not clean up hosted spaces after End space moved into the overflow menu. Open the space overflow menu before waiting for the End action.

The IoT data plane health check expected an authorization denial at the root, which returned 404 while signed publishing worked. Probe an unsigned POST to the actual publish route and require its 403 denial.

Live person probes backdated new traces to the spec's fixed evening clock, outside Tempo's searchable ingestion block range during midday Deploy runs. Anchor the live fixture at the current minute while preserving its zone and differences between evening and morning questions.

A branch-dispatched Health run could obtain its OIDC token but AWS rejected AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity because the only CI role trusted main and production; widening that deploy role would have granted feature branches mutation access. Fixed with a separate read-only health role that trusts this repository's branches, published as AWS_HEALTH_ROLE_ARN and selected only by health.yml.
Wrong moves scored zero instead of the agreed half credit; the recorder also read the move before its reactive row was available. Fixed using the board transition and guarded through offline replay.
The profile snapshot omitted Glicko volatility, leaving another device with incomplete rating state. Fixed by syncing volatility_micros and comparing complete profiles after guest sign-in.

mockingbird-postgres returned bigint for domain integer (physical bigint) columns, so the product harness's hydrate died with `Cannot convert BigInt to number`. Fixed by normalizing int8 values through decimal text.

An int8 counter upsert (`n = n + 1`) mixed a JS number and a bigint inside mockingbird-postgres and threw, so every second push on a topic failed. Fixed in the engine; allocateTopicPushSeq also uses the portable `CAST(1 AS BIGINT)`.

Repeated letters slipped past the username filter: runs of 3+ collapsed to one letter and doubles were never collapsed, so `faggggot` and `fuuck` were accepted. Fixed by matching each letter run in a term as that many or more.
Accented letters slipped past the username filter: NFKC kept `ü` composed and then dropped it as a separator, so `fück` read as `fck`. Fixed by NFKD, which strips the accent and keeps the letter.
streamParallelIndexed dropped a work unit that rejected with `undefined` — no frame was sent, so the client reported a missing result instead of the error. Fixed with an explicit ok flag.
createUuidV7 copied upper-case entropy verbatim, minting mixed-case ids whose string order disagreed with the canonical lower-case form. Fixed by lower-casing the entropy.
Avatar config serialization kept object key order inside arrays, so equal configs compared unequal and the editor could report unsaved changes. Fixed by canonicalizing recursively.
Avatar config serialization silently dropped a `__proto__` option key (assignment set the prototype). Fixed by building the result with Object.fromEntries.

createAsyncRunner: a cancelled run settling late deleted the newer run's in-flight entry for the same key, so the next run started a duplicate operation. Fixed by evicting only the entry the settling run owns.

The sync-engine harness's invariant check read client databases outside a transaction, saw an upload verdict half-applied, and raised a false permanent-vs-transient failure. Fixed by reading inside a transaction.

The Workers' compatibility_date (2026-09-22) ran ahead of the pinned wrangler 4.87's workerd (supports up to 2026-05-07), so check:api's local preview refused to boot and every deploy failed while bun check stayed green. Fixed by bumping wrangler and holding the date at or below workerd's in check:worker-bundle.

Right-drag arrows began on `contextmenu`, which Windows fires after `pointerup`, so the stroke ended before it began: right-drags drew nothing there and the next right-click drew from a stale origin. Fixed by beginning strokes on the secondary `pointerdown`.

Board move / up handlers ignored `pointerId`: a second finger steered the dragged piece and its release ended the drag as a drop on the second finger's square. Fixed by binding each press to its pointer id.
Arrow geometry was computed once per arrow, so parent-supplied arrows kept pointing the old way after the board flipped. Fixed by deriving geometry from the orientation.
Android fires `contextmenu` on a touch long-press; the board took it for a right button during a drag and put the held piece back. Fixed by cancelling on `contextmenu` only for mouse / pen presses.

Board gestures were wrapped in Solid `batch` for a single reactive flush, which also ran the parent's `onMove` inside the batch and deferred the parent's own effects; the puzzle screen's offline outcome was never recorded. Fixed by batching only transitions that cannot play a move.

`//#health` depended on bare `health`, which the root `health` script resolves back to `//#health`, so turbo refused to plan `//#deploy` ("//#health depends on itself") and every deploy failed. Fixed by dropping the one-dep `//#health` aggregator; `//#deploy` depends on `health` directly, and a graph test fails `bun check` on any root-task cycle.

Deploy died on `get stack failed: HTTP 403` for stack shortawning2091, which was read as "the stack lives in another org" and fixed by switching the slug to gamezilla. The real cause was GRAFANA_CLOUD_API_TOKEN's access policy lacking stacks:read/stacks:write: shortawning2091 is the org's own (and, on the free plan, only) stack, and creating gamezilla failed with 403 at the plan limit. Fixed by granting the stacks scopes and adopting shortawning2091 as the shared stack (libs/infra/tofu/global.tfvars.json).

When the Check run hit its hard deadline, turbo-ci-run SIGKILLed turbo and claimed turbo prints the tasks still running; it cannot, so the log said only "deadline reached" and a 207-task cache miss on a 2-core runner was indistinguishable from a wedged task. Fixed by snapshotting the process tree before the kill and printing each running task with its elapsed time and package.

The Bun.WebView driver typed only into a node that held a `value`, but `@pkgs/ui` TextInput puts its test id on the wrapper `<div>`, so `input` / `clear` / `text` on every TextInput were silent no-ops in a real browser (the Solid DOM driver resolved the nested field). Fixed by resolving the wrapper's `<input>` / `<textarea>` like the Solid DOM driver.

The Bun.WebView driver's `text()` returned any node's `value`, and every `<button>` has one (`""`), so `expect.text` on a button never matched in a real browser: the avatar "Saved" critical journey failed in production while the Solid DOM driver passed. Fixed by reading `value` only from `<input>` / `<textarea>`, else visible text, else `aria-label`, like the Solid DOM driver.

After the global CLI installer was replaced by mise, @apps/product's deploy spawned `wrangler` without declaring it, so `bun run` never put the bin on PATH and Deploy failed with `Executable not found in $PATH: "wrangler"`. Fixed by declaring wrangler in every package that spawns it; lint-package now fails a package that spawns an undeclared npm CLI.

Deploy failed at @libs/infra#apply:foundation with `missing secrets for the foundation stack`: secrets-run injected TOFU_STATE_* and NEON_API_KEY, but turbo's strict env mode dropped them because globalPassThroughEnv did not name them (SYNTHETIC_MONITOR_TOKEN too). Fixed by passing them through; every registry secret is now asserted to pass through.

Production signed-in health journeys left the initial app route immediately after document navigation, so Chrome could retain its aborted lazy import as a pending promise and return from auth to a tab shell with an empty body. Fixed by waiting for the initial tab shell before starting hosted sign-in.

The disabled performance HUD eagerly bundled its browser sampler and web-vitals attribution into the client boot path, leaving the cross-platform bundle budget without enough headroom. Fixed by loading the sampler only when the HUD is enabled.

Every browser sign-in on the deployed web app failed silently: apiCors set its headers with c.header() before next(), and Hono drops those when a handler returns a raw Response, which the auth service's handler.fetch does. POST /api/auth/session therefore reached www without Access-Control-Allow-Origin, the code exchange was blocked, and the Health workflow's signed-in journeys never passed. The harness is same-origin, so bun check could not see it. Fixed by writing the CORS headers onto the final response after next().

A `pendingUx: 'pending'` mutation reported the server's rejection before the device dropped its optimistic write, so the caller's next action ran against the refused write: a username refused as taken and then saved again at once was refused as 'changed recently'. Found by the username-changes Quint model. Fixed by settling a rejection only after the queries refresh.

After Apple deleted a connected Apple account, the person's devices kept listing Apple as a sign-in method until they signed in again or removed a method themselves: the IdP removed the identity on Apple's notification, but the product mirrors sign-in methods into the synced auth_external_accounts only on /identity/refresh, which a device runs for its own sign-ins. Fixed by the auth service telling the product (AuthProviderEnv.onUserChanged) once a notification changes a user's identities; the product re-mirrors them and pushes the user's topic.

A same-tab navigation (the sign-in callback, a reload) left the previous page owning the local database: discarded before its async disconnect told the SharedWorker broker, or frozen in the back/forward cache still holding its OPFS handles. The next page waited on the dead owner and boot hung on "Starting…" (~15s of locked-handle retries, then "did not become ready"). Fixed by releasing the store (terminating the sqlite worker) and leaving the broker synchronously on every pagehide.

A device that signed out stayed on its old account's devices list: the device row's owner moves with the install and synced rows are never removed. Fixed with a tombstoned account-device record and notifying the account the device left.
Switch put its test id on a wrapper around the toggle, so activating it by id changed nothing. Fixed by moving the identifiers onto the toggle button.

An active or trialing membership granted paid access on a device however long it had gone without confirming it. Fixed: access lapses 7 days (the grace) after the last sync and returns on the next one.
A refunded membership ended at its period end and kept paid access through the 7-day grace. Fixed: a refunded membership ends with no paid time, so no grace applies.
Access facts and the billing tier read the clock once, so grace running out never updated a screen left open. Fixed with createTimedValue, which re-reads at the instant access lapses.
Offline, once the rating crossed a band edge the feed waited forever for rating bands that could not download. Fixed: offline it falls back to the puzzles on the device.

Guests had no hosting limit and nothing enforced the free account limit of one hosted space. Fixed: guest and free are capped at 1 through the permissions evaluation on device and server; Plus is unlimited.
Feed choices were stored only on the device and never reached the player's other devices. Fixed with synced feed settings written by a mutation.
Guests could open and change the feed settings although customizing the feed is for accounts. Fixed: guests get the sign-in invitation instead.
People search waited forever without a connection. Fixed: it says search needs a connection.
A friend request sent offline was quietly queued and delivered later without the sender knowing. Fixed: it says friend requests need a connection and sends nothing.
Creating a space offline was quietly queued. Fixed: it says spaces need a connection.

A link to a missing space said it was unavailable before anything had answered, and the same while offline. Fixed: it says the space cannot be found once known, offers the way back, and offline says spaces need a connection.

ci:i18n re-extracted and recompiled the committed Lingui catalogs in place, so a tc running beside it could read a half-written messages.ts and fail with "is not a module". Fixed: the check regenerates into .cache/ci-i18n and compares.

A write that waits for the server's answer (`pendingUx: 'pending'`) could stay 'saving' forever: after the upload ack committed, recording the ack's topic push sequences raced the echoed push applying the same topic, the insert hit a UNIQUE conflict, and the ack's table-change notice (which wakes the answer) was never sent. Found porting pending-ux-answers-with-server-verdict to specs/sync-engine/checked-notes.feature. Fixed by recording a push sequence idempotently (ON CONFLICT, then raise).

A person's unacknowledged refusal notices vanished when the app updated to a version that fetches every note again, or when its data was cleared: sync_engine_write_rejections was a cache table, wiped with the fetched rows, and nothing fetches it back. Found porting the explore walks into specs/sync-engine/note-replication.qnt. Fixed by keeping it durable, like the unsent-edit queue.

Clearing the app's data while offline hid the notes the person had written but not yet sent until the device was back online: the wipe dropped the rows and nothing re-applied the queue. Found by the note-replication model. Fixed by re-applying queued edits after any wipe of the fetched rows (cleared data, an epoch bump on open).

A garbled live update (fields renamed on the way) created a note on other devices with no title or text until the next refresh. Found by the note-replication model's garbled-live-updates action. Fixed by refusing a pushed image that would create a row without every column the device keeps; the row is refetched whole.

Signing in saved the new session before the server had bound its account, so the app showed the person signed in while it still ran on the device's guest data; when the account arrived seconds later the app rebuilt under it and dropped what they had done meanwhile (a space hosted, a search typed), failing the production critical journeys. Fixed by keeping a new sign-in pending until its account is bound, then saving account and session together, with the sign-in modal on "Signing in…" until then.

Health (and any Deploy step reading secrets live) failed after its tenth minute with "Your token has expired": the CI identity's OIDC-minted Infisical token lives 600s, and the admin CLI store published it as INFISICAL_TOKEN, which the resolver then read back as the caller's own token and never minted again. Fixed by marking a minted token with its expiry (INFISICAL_TOKEN_EXPIRES_AT) and re-resolving before every CLI call, minting a new token a minute before the old one expires; a caller's own token is never replaced.

The Report workflow never succeeded: every suite passed, then report:publish died with "Could not find an existing 'wrangler' binary to run". The job runs `report-publish.ts` from the repo root, where the isolated linker links no wrangler bin (only packages that declare it get one), and a laptop's global wrangler hid it. Fixed by running wrangler from @libs/tools, which declares it. The wrangler upload is gone (reports now reach the shared store over S3); the guard covers the publish step's other linked tool, the Tailwind CLI that builds the snapshot stylesheet.

A Health run's prd job hung and GitHub cancelled it at its 20-minute job timeout with no output, so nobody learned which probe hung: turbo-ci-run's own CI deadline (1200 s) could never fire first, because setup ate into the same 20 minutes. check.yml and deploy.yml already kept their timeouts above the deadline; health.yml now does too (a 25-minute step timeout inside a 30-minute job).

The people search query (searchProfiles) had no authorize hook, and the sync server only refuses callers with no actor id, so a guest's install got search results from the server although the app hides search from guests. Fixed by authorizing the query through the permission layer (people:search). Found by the access decision table's server layer.

leaveSpace took no permission decision and requireSpacePermission treated every non-host as a member, so someone not in a space got a silent success instead of being refused. Fixed by deciding the person's place in the space (host, joined, not in it) through the permission layer. Found by the space-roles decision table.

ratePuzzleAttempt recorded a rated result without checking the rated-puzzle quota ledger, so a guest past the 20-a-day limit (a client that skipped or replayed past the refused consume) still got rated results recorded on the server. Fixed with requireChargedInMutation: a rated result needs a charged start unless the person has no limit. Found by the daily-puzzle-limit decision table.

After Apple deleted an account's only Apple account, the server ended every session but kept each device's live auth_account_devices row, and a device kept its own live row after any sign-out because it only synced the rows of the account it was in. Fixed by tombstoning every membership of an account left with no sign-in method in the same transaction, and syncing each device its own memberships in every account. Found by the accounts Alloy structure audit.

The bottom tab bar exposed role=tablist with plain buttons and no tab children, so a listener heard an empty tab list (ACT bc4a75, WCAG 1.3.1). Fixed by dropping the role: the bar is a nav of buttons with aria-current.

The avatar on a person's own profile was drawn as a decorative image (alt=""), so a listener heard nothing for it (ACT 23a2a8, WCAG 1.1.1). Fixed by ProfileAvatarFigure: one role=img named "Your avatar".

Navigating between screens (opening Settings from the account menu, coming back) dropped keyboard focus to the start of the page (WCAG 2.4.3). Fixed in ScreenBase/AppFrame: the next screen takes focus on its title, or back on the control the person left it from.

Menu rows were named by their label alone ("Theme" for a row showing "Theme System") and the Connectivity row by its status alone ("Online"), so a listener did not hear the visible label (ACT 2ee8b8, WCAG 2.5.3). Fixed: a row's name comes from what it shows unless an aria-label is authored; the Connectivity row authors none.

The space room's select-game command was accepted from anyone connected (the room route is open to anyone and no command gate existed), so a joined member or someone not in the space could make the game choice; only the host (spaces:select-game) may. Fixed: the room gateway decides the actor's space grants through the permission layer at upgrade, strips any client-supplied grants, and the room refuses SelectGame without them. Found by the space-roles decision table.

The server hashed a scope's Postgres rows (booleans, jsonb objects and scalars) while the client re-hashed the same rows read back from SQLite (1, JSON text, and a jsonb scalar in a TEXT column read back as text), so ownUser, ownProfile and clientConfig never read as in sync. Every sweep healed them with a refetch, sweeps ran back to back, and "New space" hung on "Opening…" in production. Fixed: both sides hash each value as the client's SQLite stores it, as text.

refreshQueries() resolved only once no sweep was pending, so sweeps enqueued after it (drift heals, pushes) held it forever and the "New space" connection check never returned. Fixed: it resolves once the sweep that carries its wake finishes.

The Bun.WebView driver read a button's text with innerText, which includes the invisible (aria-hidden, opacity-0) idle label that keeps a feedback button's width, so the avatar button read "Save Saved" and the production "Saved" critical journey never passed while the Solid DOM driver, which skips aria-hidden branches, did. Fixed: the WebView driver skips the same hidden branches.

The production monitor account hosts one live space at a time. Critical journeys that died after creating a space left it live, so the next create was the Plus invitation and the journey never entered a space. Fixed: hosting ends those leftover spaces first, and the cleanup is registered before the create so a later failure still ends the new one.

Ending leftover hosted spaces treated a missing hosting count as hosting none. That count is also missing while the spaces list is still syncing, so a journey created another space before the server's live one arrived. The server refused the create, and the device was left on the join screen of a space it was no longer in. Fixed: wait until the list has answered, including when the count is zero, and wait for that answer again before creating.

An anonymous critical journey started hosting as soon as the document navigated, before the tab shell existed, and then waited the whole step on a back button that was not on screen. By the time that wait ended, the Spaces tab was already up. Fixed: every journey waits for the tab shell, and a missing back button waits for the screen itself.

After a host entered their space, a later sync could tombstone that device's open session while the space stayed live, and the join screen still offered a tombstoned space as live. The host could not end the space or keep a puzzle on screen. Fixed: a tombstoned space is not a live join, and a host whose own session was tombstoned on a live space reopens it.

pressBackUntilVisible spent its whole timeout tapping nav-back even when that control was not on screen, so a screen that appeared during the wait was never noticed. Fixed: with no back control, wait for the destination itself.

A fresh device opening a leftover hosted space lands on Join, because that device has no open session, and End exists only after joining. The journey looked for End immediately and timed out, so the monitor account stayed at its hosting limit. Fixed: when Join is on screen, join the space, then end it.

The reports API Worker bundled the AWS SDK browser XML parser, which constructs DOMParser. workerd has none, so listing the reports bucket threw and /api/reports was 500 (the screen said it could not reach the API). Fixed by installing xmldom's DOMParser only when the runtime does not already have one, before the S3 client is used.

Critical journeys left the monitor account on the join screen of its own live space, where End is not shown. Join waited on a query sweep with no deadline, so the button stayed on Joining and the space stayed live for the next run. Deploy and Health then failed the same way every time. Fixed: a host looking at their own live space is taken inside, and the connection check stops waiting after a few seconds.

A Railway GraphQL client error while reading EMQX_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD failed the drift check as if the environment had been changed by hand. The plan produced no diff; the provider connection dropped. Fixed: a plan read that fails with a transient provider error is tried again.

People search kept one rate-limit map for the whole process, keyed only by account id. Parallel spec harnesses share that process and quint traces mint the same account ids, so one trace used up the budget and a later search came back empty. Fixed: each server's clock has its own bucket.

People search kept the previous person on screen while a new username was still settling, and the list shell can be in the DOM before any row paints. The harness treated that as a finished search and stopped advancing virtual time, so the next step waited on the wall clock for a button the debounce never painted. Fixed: an in-flight search shows Searching, a search counts only once a row or a real empty, offline, or sign-in answer is painted, the keystroke debounce is advanced before that check, and Add, open, and unblock keep the clock moving until their own control is on screen.

People search counted every keystroke and every refetch toward a 30-a-minute cap, then answered the next name with an empty list. The screen said nobody was found, so Add never appeared. A friendship trace moves virtual time between letters and refetches the open search, and one person spent the whole budget that way. Fixed: a name already counted in the window still runs, and typing a name is one change rather than one search per letter.

Scrolling while bun check, bun health, or bun deploy watched a GitHub run printed a stream of ^[[B. A scroll wheel sends down-arrow keys, and the watcher left the terminal echoing input, so those keys landed in the transcript. Fixed by turning echo off for the watch and discarding the keys, then restoring the terminal.

A newer push cancelled Check's shards, but publish, close, and the verdict use if: always(), so they kept running and held the check-<pr> concurrency group. The required check on the new commit stayed queued and the PR stayed blocked. Fixed by skipping those jobs when the run is cancelled; a red shard is not a cancellation, so the report and the verdict still run.

Model and release checks could accept safety evidence while declared temporal properties were never checked. TLC now checks finite graphs and the conformance verdict requires every declared temporal obligation. A safe model with permanently unreachable completion is pinned as the regression.

A requested inductive candidate was ignored by the model verifier, allowing ordinary safety evidence to stand in for an unbounded proof. The verifier now requires initialization, transition preservation, and implication; a candidate broken by opening a safe door is pinned.

The TLC evidence reader took the first progress count instead of the completed graph, reporting a varying partial size as exhaustive evidence. It now requires successful graph completion, an empty final queue, and the final count and search depth. The literal 13,084-to-19,000 output is pinned.

The executable blocking adapter required an existing friendship, leaving blocking strangers and pending outgoing requests unverified. The adapter now opens the person through search and uses the general blocking action. Both literal failing scenarios are pinned.

Rated puzzle entitlement conformance still read solved counts after the product promise changed to charge quota when a rated puzzle starts. The decision bindings now consume start counts at the exact day boundary; the failing literal 0 today and 100 earlier input is pinned.

Partitioned product clients still received in-memory live events, so offline relationship traces used current server knowledge. Events now respect the same reachability gate as HTTP and room connections, drop changes during a cut, and signal reconnect so sync can repair. The literal before/offline/after sequence is pinned.

Reconnecting devices downloaded only blocks they created, missing incoming blocks or their removal while offline. The block snapshot now includes both parties and tombstones, preserving search privacy and allowing recovery after unblock. Literal block and unblock during the other device outage are pinned.

People search returned the blocker profile to a blocked actor and relied on a possibly stale client-side filter. The server query now withholds active blockers while preserving discovery in the unblock direction and profile tombstones needed for synchronization. Alice blocking Bob is the literal regression.

The sent-event consumer published a live friend-request notification after cancellation committed first. Independent outbox deliveries could therefore revive a closed request. The consumer now checks the current pending request and its exact id before publishing.

Stepping out to the lobby retained a live room connection, leaving people counted as present despite the space promise. Room lifetime now follows actual space views, while membership, queued commands and the open-session identity survive stepping out. The literal friend-step-out sequence is pinned.

The presence sheet and avatar strip used a stale room roster while disconnected. They now require a connected, caught-up room before presenting current presence. Losing Bob’s connection while in Alice’s space is pinned.

The in-process room admission adapter could finish registering a connection after it had been destroyed, creating a ghost connection or taking over a newer open. Admission now honors cancellation before registration. Destroy-before-admission-completes is pinned.

An initial room admission failure left a failed transport installed forever, preventing the heartbeat from retrying after the joined membership reached the server. The first failure now clears and destroys that transport so recovery can open a fresh connection. One failure followed by a heartbeat is pinned.

Leaving a space navigated through browser history, so joining from a link could send the person to an unrelated screen and hide the outcome. Guests now remain on the open space with an offer to join again; hosts remain on the ended space. Bob joining by link and then leaving is pinned.

Space room session identities were kept in a process-wide map, so independent app roots with the same install and space keys reused one root’s room identity. The store now belongs to the app provider, preserving its own identity across detail remounts and clearing closed memberships even after stepping out. Two roots with distinct id ports and identical keys are pinned.

Replay accepted a trace that read one correct field while omitting another public model promise. Every public state variable must now be read from the product before a trace can pass. A door whose last actor is never observed is the literal regression.

The wording gate collapsed different actor/device parameter types, pending/completed saves and immediate/once-only visibility into aliases. It now retains these substantive distinctions while detecting true filler aliases. All three literal false-alias pairs are pinned.

Interruption between appending a puzzle outcome and rating the attempt left a permanent rating gap because retry exited when it saw the outcome. Retrying now offers the first recorded outcome to the idempotent rating mutation. The literal interrupted solved attempt is pinned.

A puzzle result arriving while the solver app is closed has no live status transition to record when restored. The original result, including wrong moves and hints, must survive and be recorded exactly once on return. Each of the five literal finish paths is pinned.

Two starts of the same puzzle at the same clock time shared the attempt key. The persisted start command identity now identifies the attempt, survives retries and differs for a fresh start. Both literal starts at 1700000000000 are pinned.

The harness room transport factory rejected construction while offline, so the saved board never opened and reconnection could not recover a finished attempt. Only connection attempts now fail while disconnected; local hydration and heartbeat recovery remain available. Finish as the app closes, reopen offline, then reconnect is pinned.

After a finish arrived while the app was closed, reopening offline and going to stats as the connection returned disposed the board recorder before it heard the result. Result reconciliation now lives across chess menu, stats and settings navigation; the literal close, offline return, reconnect and stats sequence is pinned.

Own-profile, profile-by-id and friendship snapshots omitted the normalized username used by the local uniqueness constraint. A rename could leave the old name reserved on another device and collide when that name was assigned elsewhere. Every profile snapshot now carries the normalized name. The literal alice_old to ALICE_NEW change is pinned through both public profile queries.

Result finalization queued an outcome and its rating as separate mutations. Failure before the second write stranded a completed outcome without a rating. One mutation now records the outcome, first rating and upload together. Literal interruption before the write and during profile persistence proves rollback and exact-once recovery.

The rating mutation accepted full credit for a failed result, zero credit for a solve and partial credit for an abandoned attempt. It now rejects outcome and credit combinations that the puzzle rules exclude, before any result is stored. All three literal contradictory combinations are pinned.

An interrupted room commit saved its events without the first retry verdict; restarting and retrying Alice's one add counted it twice. Room storage now atomically persists the complete event batch and verdict, including batches larger than 128 keys.

Losing the storage acknowledgement after a room commit left the live engine and storage tip stale; the next legitimate change failed with expected sequence 1, got 2. Reload committed state and invalidate the storage tip after an ambiguous commit failure.

An accepted timed-match start or move survived in the room log without its timeout effect. Recovery now restores the original absolute deadline from committed match state, including when no player remains connected.
The room-crash fault disconnected players but left the old authoritative timer running, concealing missing schedule recovery. A stopped server now disposes its timer before advancing virtual time.

A timeout whose event write aborted could restore the same deadline against an already consumed wake, leaving the match permanently playing. Wake execution now rearms before injection and preserves failed and not-yet-executed deadlines.
Concurrent results from separate devices could overwrite the running rating with two events based on the same prior value.
A permanent refusal after earlier domain writes committed those writes instead of rolling them back.
Production replay did not supply the authoritative server clock to time-sensitive mutation bodies.
Bun exposes the PostgreSQL SQLSTATE as errno, so mapped permanent constraint refusals were treated as retryable failures.
Optimistic row fanout published a checked draft before acceptance, allowing refused writing onto another person's device.
An unparenthesized Boolean assignment compiled into an additional action guard, silently omitting accepted writes from the proof graph.
The permission conformance catalog still named solving a rated puzzle while the specification charges access when the rated puzzle starts.
The manifest declared account deletion and personal-data exports without corresponding permission keys, capability mappings, or account-only policy grants.

A rulebook change used a docs subject instead of spec, violating ownership. Reworded the commit and keyed the ownership gate on the injected full-SHA range so local history changes cannot reuse an earlier verdict.
The model discovery regression expected the old sync model list after note-refusal-recovery was added, rejecting correct discovery of the new bounded model.

The username model binding signed in Alice and Bob but left their generated names in place, diverging at init from the model's named accounts. Setup now saves the required names through the profile UI before recording any model action.
The evidence map omitted five declared device environments and the privacy and developer-tools public contracts, leaving the conformance manifest without proof mappings.
Profile card and display reads returned a retained soft-deleted profile. All display reads now exclude tombstones while sync snapshots still carry them.
Anonymous session recovery reused a proposed deleted account ID and repeatedly failed authentication. Deleted account IDs now mint a fresh anonymous identity.
Deliveries ignored the event availability time, immediately running future work including 30-day erasure. Deliveries now inherit the event deadline.
Adding managed INSERT timestamps appended their bindings after ON CONFLICT parameters, assigning Preparing to a timestamp and blocking server exports. Bindings now follow their SQL positions.

The workload index parser assigned a joined device filter to the deletion receipts table, so localhost startup failed creating an index on a nonexistent device_id column. Columns now resolve through each SELECT's table aliases, including join predicates.
An install header without a verified bearer could authenticate its signed-in account owner.
A worker claimed deliveries for absent consumers and other event partitions, consuming attempts without running the owner.
The harness request database middleware returned from finally, suppressing route exceptions and returning empty HTTP 200 bodies.
A revoked token from a deleted account fell back to a new anonymous owner on mutation replay; deletion history is checked after fresh bearer verification and before anonymous mutation fallback.

A provider callback could revive a subscription if deletion committed after the callback read the linked account. Guard the projection with the durable closure journal in the INSERT statement; closed accounts settle payments without projecting membership.
Expanded examples of a Scenario Outline with a constant title were mistaken for duplicate declarations. Duplicate checks now use the source declaration while preserving each example line.
Registering the developer-tools harness replaced the live health host in the same entry. World lifecycles can now select their scenarios and an unmatched scenario keeps the default live host.
Reconciling framework tables dropped unique indexes owned by domain tables. The SQLite planner now removes stale indexes only for the slice it owns.
A partial or pending provider refund was reported as completed withdrawal. Settlement now rereads payment totals and keeps withdrawal pending until every later payment is fully returned.
Individually bounded diagnostics could collectively exceed the reporting HTTP limit and reject the basic report. Enforce a total UTF-8 diagnostic budget and mark excess context unavailable.
An HTTP transport or response body ignoring AbortSignal left reporting pending forever. A hard deadline now preserves the emergency recovery path.

The feedback Vite plugin eagerly imported workspace runtime TypeScript while Node evaluated the build config, so its extensionless imports failed with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Load the dev backend through Vite only when configuring the dev server.
Social sign-in depended on window.open, which IDE integrated browsers and popup-blocking browsers refused. Navigate the current tab and complete sign-in on the callback route instead.

The same-tab OAuth callback discarded provider errors and pending account-link prompts, leaving resumed sign-in without its result. Publish every callback failure to the auth session for the existing modal.
A discarded recording finishing asynchronously could dispose and overwrite a newly started video session. Retire the captured session and ignore completions from an old recording generation.

Chess square hit buttons take no pointer events and the board captures the pointer. Recording only square targets dropped real chess drags. Preserve board control identifiers and normalized pointer endpoints.
An upload response body ignoring cancellation could keep feedback sending indefinitely after the network request completed. Bound the complete upload and receipt read with the same hard deadline.

Adding evidence after an uncertain delivery could reuse the archived report id and leave the updated recording out of the saved bundle. Preserve ids for unchanged retries and mint a new id for edited evidence.

Initial product state could be captured before a person finished choosing the screen, while the product continued to change. Capture the starting position after the chooser resolves, and release video immediately if recording is cancelled during context collection.

Each feedback answer edit invalidated the dialog visibility dependency even though it stayed open, restarting focus handling and moving focus to Close. Memoize visibility independently of draft updates so typing keeps field focus.
An attachment finishing after a new draft was selected could persist in the newly selected draft. Capture the initiating document and commit evidence only to that document.
Reopening after an uncertain submission discarded the attempted report id and could create duplicate feedback. Journal attempted reports and recover their ids for unchanged retries.

A failed feedback submission exposed the browser's raw "Load failed" transport error and expanded a large emergency payload, even though the draft was safely journalled. Fixed by presenting a concise recovery state, keeping the draft editable, and moving the machine-readable recovery payload behind an explicit disclosure.

The shipped client TypeScript configuration omitted the OPFS package path used by the feedback browser root, so a cold app type-check could not resolve evidence storage. Keep the concrete feedback import resolvable through the client path map.

Buttons without an explicit type inside the feedback form inherited HTML's submit default, so choosing a template sent the draft. The shared Button now defaults to type=button and only explicit submit controls submit forms.

The feedback widget clamp assumed the widget was shorter than the viewport, so a tall resized editor forced y=0 and left its grab handle above the visible area. Fixed by allowing the bottom-anchored widget to translate downward when only its header can fit.

The first Neki foundation plan configured the PostgreSQL provider from a role that the same plan had not created yet. OpenTofu substituted localhost and failed before it could create the database; the transition also tried to delete the retired broker's random credentials. Fixed by leaving pg_stat_statements with Neki's PlanetScale-managed default profile, removing the cyclic provider, and forgetting retired credentials without destroying them.

The Neki branch used AWS's region name us-east-1, but PlanetScale's organization catalog names that region with the slug us-east. The API rejected the first branch with HTTP 422 after other foundation resources had already applied. Fixed by keeping AWS IoT on us-east-1 while passing PlanetScale's us-east slug to Neki.

Foundation wrote the new Neki DATABASE_URL, but the migration task preferred the stale process value injected before foundation ran. Worker deploy refreshed its secrets and connected to the new empty database, so readiness and auth failed because client_config did not exist. Fixed by preferring the live post-foundation secret while retaining the injected URL as an offline fallback.

The first schema reconcile on Neki stopped at ALTER COLUMN SET STORAGE with NK013 because Neki cannot preserve that storage setting as shards join. Catching it inside the schema transaction still left the transaction aborted, and after commit the router could briefly return 42P01 for the newly created table. Fixed by committing required schema first, then applying optional storage tuning in autocommit, where explicit unsupported errors are skipped and temporary table visibility defers tuning without hiding unrelated failures.
The issue list grew with its content and stage changes left keyboard focus on removed controls.
The issue detail hid its only two actions behind an unnecessary menu.
Evidence controls had pointer-only labels clipped by the editor frame.
Typing a complete slash command expanded it before acceptance, with no keyboard suggestions.

The root crash screen discarded the selected theme and rendered hardcoded red colors. Keep the minimal theme root mounted above recovery and render themed, responsive recovery controls with expandable diagnostics.
Crash recovery reported a successful copy without a clipboard and left denied writes unhandled. Use the injected clipboard, show retryable copy feedback, and cancel feedback timers on recovery.

Adding privacy decisions caused every mounted permission conformance probe to throw because its auth client provider was absent. Ordinary grant hooks now initialize privacy dependencies only for privacy actions, and conformance mounts the auth port alongside its existing providers.

The report publisher silently skipped a missing referenced snapshot and still published its source as complete. Fail publication before writing any completion marker when the literal referenced snapshot is absent.

Two Check runs of the same SHA wrote the same report source and completion record, so a late failed earlier attempt could overwrite the currently displayed result. Scope commit records, stylesheet, sources and receipts by run/attempt while sharing only immutable successful content.
Completed commit URLs cached a prior attempt forever, even after a newer run replaced the selected report. Resolve the selected attempt on every request to these mutable URLs.

A task could execute under a different hash from the preflight plan and publish its evidence under the earlier hash. Verify Turbo's execution or restoration hash before publishing the completed source.

A native Depot CI migration left Check under .github/workflows requesting Depot managed GitHub runners, so no native workflow owned its trigger. Keep Check, Deploy and Health only under .depot/workflows and dispatch native runs.
Native Check requested .depot/actions/setup after checkout but the manifest was absent from that revision. Verify the complete local-action reference graph, including nested manifests.
The native CI migration changed the workflow path to .depot/workflows/check.yml, but git-sync classified it as chore instead of ci. Classify both CI providers' configuration paths as ci changes.

The Infisical token refresh appended &audience to an OIDC request URL without a query, treating the audience as part of the path. Set the URL search parameter and derive the audience from the new repository owner.

The availability objective kept reading GitHub Actions history after native Depot migration, losing the new Health checks. Read every native run page and every job attempt, including failed originals and successful reruns.

The transferred repository has no main branch protection rule, but bootstrap kept the old gamezilla:main adoption ID and failed to plan. Remove the completed import so the declared rule is created for the new owner.
Turbo strict environment mode dropped native Depot context, including report attempt URLs and the token needed for CI history. Pass Depot variables to tasks without changing task hashes.

The default map encoding exceeded the existing 120-second budget for index-reconciliation.qnt at ten steps. Opt this supported reference model into array-encoded maps, preserving every invariant and the full bound.

Bootstrap created four Depot variables concurrently for gamezilla-org/gamezilla. One succeeded and three failed to create their variants. Provision all four coordinates sequentially in one declared resource.

At its existing one-step bound, note-replication.qnt exhausted 240 seconds checking every invariant independently for each transition. Check invariants after the complete transition choice, preserving every reachable state and retaining default map encoding for higher-order models.

Native Check failed before running checks because the Infisical action omitted the required OIDC audience. Its bundled client also appends &audience to Depot's queryless token URL. Supply the repository-owner audience matching the declared trust and start the query before invoking the action.

The OIDC action regression redirected GITHUB_ENV to /dev/stdout, which cannot be opened when the Linux test runner captures stdout with a socket. Execute the action with a real temporary environment file and read it through stdout instead.

A full Check with cache reads disabled ran all 489 tasks successfully but failed report publication. The stream verified task hashes only for Turbo's cache hit and miss messages, ignoring cache bypass, force executing. Recognize bypass messages while preserving exact planned-hash verification and waiting for completion before uploading.

The eight-day billing grace scenario failed when a callback enqueued a task due at 1718409601001 while the duration drain yielded at virtual time 1718409935000. The drain tried to rewind the clock to the overdue deadline. Fire overdue work at the current time and advance only to future deadlines.

A diagnostic Check override used local:w,remote:w, which disables cache reads. Enforce local:rw,remote:rw after secrets injection for normal checks and verify actual Turbo remote restoration and write-only bypass.
actions/cache rejects Depot API events without GITHUB_REF. Remove redundant dependency-tree and install-store actions; cold frozen installs took 1.62 seconds.
The preflight remote HEAD lookup could turn a non-cacheable task into a hit. Honor resolvedTaskDefinition.cache so live advisory data is checked on every run.

Builds omitted baked-in commit hash/date, ANALYZE, toolchain pins and shared Lingui config from hashes. Offline-shell verification also hashed generated dist before its build dependency restored it. Hash source inputs and rely on the build dependency for generated output identity.

Report publication labeled captured timeline count as test count. Six passing framework spec suites with no timelines appeared to execute zero tests. Label timelines accurately and preserve their tests.
An over-sharded or misconfigured empty spec part exited successfully and published a passing completion. Fail with a configuration error so the empty task is removed or its scope repaired.

Concurrent Depot runs injected remote S3 credentials into a cached contract suite and reused its seeded namespace. The listKeys example saw a/x, a/y, b, k instead of a/x, a/y, b. Always run against a private local S3rver and create a fresh seeded prefix for every test.

Cached Postgres and EMQX contracts selected external services from unhashed injected credentials, making passes stale and writing shared infrastructure. Always use private local sidecars. Pin unreachable injected endpoints in the contract fixture isolation check.

The consolidated application deployment depended directly on the root Check aggregator. Turbo bypassed the runner's aggregator flattening and tried to schedule missing root lint/test tasks, failing before any deployment. Keep Check in the release runner and pin the exact retirement dependency chain as a dry-run regression.
The S3 adapter accepted an HttpClient but used the SDK wall transport, making injected transport tests and clients ineffective. Send every S3 request through the injected handler.
Check uploaded every individual report snapshot again, including cached suites, incurring millions of paid R2 writes. Publish compressed, bounded chunks and reuse identical chunks on reruns.
The reports store retained superseded commits and reports of merged or deleted branches for thirty days. Keep only one report per existing branch and garbage collect orphan uploads.

Check run 36975436667 passed every shard but its final job exceeded 10 minutes pruning reports. Commit 075ee6c683761e1b2173d33aa0d0ccfebdb404ea alone contained 56,999 objects under one hash partition. Split large trees into concurrent child listings, but read small subtrees in one page: walking 128 individual snapshot folders otherwise took 387 requests.

The repository model-shape test omitted the registered system campaign and treated every imported helper as a standalone aggregate. Require explicit campaign discovery at every call; unregistered modules still fail aggregate checks, while campaign checks remain separately required.

Moving composed Quint models under specs/system broke the closed-world adapter, which demanded standalone product contexts and bindings. Registered campaigns now retain gated specification-only coverage, including transitive imported-module evidence, without claiming a product trace adapter. Ungated campaigns and missing evidence still fail.

Subscription callbacks fetched unrelated payment history, so a valid provider-switch callback could fail before projecting membership. Payment notifications fetch payment evidence; membership notifications only project guarded membership changes.

Signed Paddle transaction.completed events were ignored, preventing payment evidence and post-deletion refund processing. Subscribe to the documented event and route its customer to the shared payment handler.

Moving the username initialization regression into the regular test leaf exposed that the leaf loaded Solid but not the product harness host. Load the harness preload so named account initialization runs against its required in-process session.

Induction spent its time limit expanding an implication already proven by named conjuncts in the candidate. Use Quint AST conjunction elimination for those exact properties; still prove the full candidate initially and under every step, and retain solver implications for every other requested property.

Concurrent TLC checks started their Apalache compiler servers on the shared default port 8822 and failed to bind. Give every temporal check its own free port and process group, matching symbolic checks.
Concurrent devices shared a process-global signup handle, causing one profile bootstrap to consume another device’s chosen name. Scope pending handles to the owning auth client.

Profile bootstrap replaced the chosen signup username with an OAuth subject such as bob-gmail-com. Provider identifiers are not usernames: retain the account’s validated choice and deny anonymous or unknown account bootstrap claims.

Opening or restoring a concurrent harness changed the global epoch used by an existing harness, recreating its client environment and auth port under a foreign durable namespace. Allocate unique epochs globally but keep each current epoch owned by its harness; checkpoint capture and restore use that same owner.

Profile bootstrap could consume the pending signup handle while the device was still bound to its anonymous identity, leaving the new account with a generated name. Keep the handoff pending until the auth bridge has persisted the verified external identity after account readiness.

Preparing a named friend read the profile handle while the spaces tab was open, mistook the absent control for an unset username, and attempted a forbidden rename of an offline recipient. Read the existing name from the profile tab before deciding whether setup needs a rename.

An approved 200 minor-unit refund of a 700 minor-unit membership item blocked the remaining 500 and the untouched 300 minor-unit item forever. Return each remaining tax-inclusive balance; pending approval still prevents a duplicate adjustment.

The unchanged specs/friends/friendship.qnt induction proof exceeded its 240-second deadline when its twelve transitions were combined into one solver formula during the full Check. Check every transition separately and discharge direct named conjuncts structurally while retaining candidate initialization and preservation; a closed-to-open counterexample guards the covered-target path.

The Alice device ignored the requested user id and shared one SQLite file between deleted-account and fresh-account, so an old alice profile blocked hydration of the fresh account with a unique username violation. Match production by retaining one file per device and account; inspection follows the active account while existing connections keep their original file.

The 600-second deadline killed only the Turbo process group, leaving detached task group 46346 and Bun worker 46357 running and writing the same report buckets during later checks. Snapshot the owned descendant tree and stop children before the root, including separate process groups and excluding concurrent checks.

The friends suite placed three 64-trace, 32-step models into four parts with sixteen traces per file; all four parts were still running past seven minutes when Check reached its 600-second deadline. Preserve every trace and seed while splitting models into eight files and the friends and chess suites into eight balanced parts.

A merge appended test:spec:6 and test:spec:7 after the package checks instead of beside the other six spec parts, breaking the exact Check and Deploy graph contracts. Keep all eight spec leaves together without removing any task.

Account sign-in trace 8 at seed 0x67932 signed Alice out offline and then timed out waiting for auth-method-google after reconnection: the harness threw HarnessPartitionedError and exposed an always-available origin, so anonymous account recovery stopped. Classify simulated HTTP failures and provide the same health-based recovery port used by the production auth bridge.

Check run 36969157332 for e483164a3 failed with Infisical Access denied: OIDC subject not allowed after the repository moved to gamezilla-org/gamezilla. The global bootstrap inputs still declared crvouga/gamezilla, producing the former subject and audience. Declare gamezilla-org so the human bootstrap apply updates Infisical and AWS trust to the transferred repository.

Check run 36971653610 failed with OIDC subject not allowed because live CI auth still trusted repo:gamezilla-org/gamezilla:*. Bootstrap could not apply the immutable subject: the auth resource was renamed from ci to github without preserving its state address, retired Depot resources were scheduled for deletion, and gamezilla:main was imported despite no protection rule existing. Keep the auth address, forget retired resources without destruction, and create the missing rule instead of importing it.

Check run 36974271617 shard 2 failed when identity-machine's 200-sample, 80-step safety exploration wrote identity-machine-last.itf.json into a missing .cache/harness-report/models directory. The evidence recorder creates that directory only after the run completes. Create the trace output directory before invoking Quint, including on fresh CI checkouts.

Check run 36974271617 failed the offline people search and invite-link scenarios: HttpNetworkError resolved parameterized queries' waitForFirstSync, clearing search's pending state and marking an unanswered invite missing. Settle failed network attempts only for session startup queries; parameterized lookups remain pending until the server answers and still complete after reconnection.

Check run 36974271617 exceeded the 600s task cap: friends part 8 took 1,075s for two eight-trace model slices, while sync-engine part 0 took 635s for its entire suite. Split the same 64 traces per model into two-trace files, distribute friends across 64 cached parts and sync across four, and retain every trace exactly once.

Check run 36977052636 shard 1 exhausted a shared 120,000ms test deadline while type-checking twelve composed product roots, reporting adversarial-examples.qnt as failed without a CLI diagnostic. Give each root and its transitive imports one independent test under the same deadline, and retain the reachability check that rejects unchecked import cycles.

Open: Check run 36977052636 shard 0 timed out symbolic identity, replication, access, multiplayer and privacy checks at 120,000ms, then reached the 1,200s shard deadline. The literal offline-replication model with its existing three-client symbolic bound and two transitions also times out in isolation: Snowcat finishes but InlinePass does not. Disabling polymorphic inference does not resolve it. Requires compiler/model optimization that preserves the declared bounds, transitions and invariants; the checks remain enabled and failing.

Check run 36974006709 failed with Infisical HTTP 403 after the repository transfer enabled GitHub's immutable OIDC subject. Bind Infisical and AWS CI identities to repo:gamezilla-org@336801040/gamezilla@1165464734 while preserving branch and environment restrictions.

The final development rehearsal resolved retirement's bare health dependency to a nonexistent @libs/infra#health task, so retirement ran alongside @apps/product#health instead of waiting for its verdict. Depend on the explicit application health task and verify the resolved Turbo graph contains that executable dependency.

Branch cleanup only listed commit-local files after reports gained attempt isolation and shared content. Preserve the selected attempt and its referenced snapshots, remove superseded attempts and orphan content, and defer shared-content cleanup while a publisher is still running.

Depot Deploy workflow ng4sv2f3d0 failed at apply:foundation because the live AWS CI roles still trusted only GitHub. The Depot OIDC provider existed outside bootstrap state, so a normal apply would attempt to recreate it before updating trust. Adopt the existing provider through global_imports and apply the declared, main-restricted Depot deploy trust and branch-readable health trust.

Stepping back after a solve changes the displayed status to solving; leaving at that position preserved the completed puzzle and offered it again on return. Completion must survive historical viewing.

The capability catalog required assistant-observation, a semantic decision with no permission answer, to own an access capability. Only decisions answering access yes/no belong in that permission catalog; every semantic decision remains bound and checked by its owner.
Reviewing a solved puzzle preserved its completed result but offered no forward control to return to the final position. Solved and skipped boards now expose bounded position navigation.

The real puzzle harness pressed the escalating hint control three times even when a hint had already been taken, then waited for a control removed by showing the solution. Stop pressing once the solution is revealed; the literal model history is pinned.

Editing the puzzle feed wrote each preview directly to synced account settings, so closing without saving retained an unconfirmed offset. Keep a local draft and persist it only on save; pool previews use the draft.

The first isolated feed draft saved only changes included in the puzzle-selection fingerprint, dropping auto-advance preferences. Persist every changed choice while selecting a different puzzle only for selection changes. The literal failing trace is pinned.
Submitting a move or requesting a hint while viewing an earlier position applied a move or revealed the opponent move. Only the current solving position can accept either action.
A raw hint command after a wrong move bypassed the required retry and changed help on the wrong-state board.
A raw solution-move command materialized the first hint and solution together, bypassing the declared help progression.

The conformance inventory treated every DMN decision without a capability input as an access decision, so assistant observation policy required an invented permission. Classify access decisions by their declared yes/no answer; keep semantic decisions bound and checked in the inventory.

The model could only inspect stored allowance rows because a limited solver could not read how many rated puzzles remained. Render the permission decision’s remaining allowance and bind the model to that visible count.

Repeating the first-hint command either restarted the same help or replaced a solution arrow with a highlight. The first hint is available only before help; later help cannot be overwritten by that earlier command.

The permission-enforcement report required a server authorization agreement from the grounded assistant semantic decision, despite its having no access capability. Require server enforcement for exactly the decision specs referenced by the capability manifest, while still checking implementation agreement for every semantic decision.

Health imported the assembled in-process browser product before its Solid/Lingui preload executed, so every live stub failed to load. Select the live world at the one registration entry without loading the browser composition; pin the actual live entry import in a child-process regression.

Applying browser resolution conditions to the live Health server process made the AWS S3 client warning export a Symbol and prevented transport construction. Select the live world using Node conditions, while in-process browser specs retain their documented Solid preload.

Health chose dev when SECRETS_ENV was absent but did not forward that resolved name to its child process, so the infrastructure check refused to run. Pin the missing environment input and verify the actual live process receives dev.

The conformance reporter read live feature reports but omitted the adjacent health-objectives-report bucket, losing recorded OpenSLO evidence. Discover both live report kinds while excluding ad-hoc harness runs.

The full-solution room command bypassed the unavailable help control while reviewing an earlier position and finished the attempt. Require the current solving position before showing a solution; retain the literal navigation and review history that exposed the gap.
Disabling new personal annotations also prevents choosing a piece from clearing completed personal marks.
Widths outside the playable range accept moves and retain selection or promotion after shrinking.
An empty en passant destination is painted as a quiet move rather than a capture.
Activity-supplied feedback text is ignored in the visible badge.
Promotion choices expose abbreviations and cancellation leaves keyboard focus at the destination.
Repeated input queues the same waiting move twice and duplicates its visual preview.
ITF decoding rejects ordered lists emitted by Quint, preventing promotion and premove trace replay.
Non-finite dimensions and pointer coordinates can manufacture invalid algebraic squares.
Scaled boards use unscaled client dimensions for pointer hit testing, disagreeing with the painted far files.
Fill-width measurement rounds to eight device pixels while CSS keeps the full fractional parent width.
Local board models are rejected for having no connection dependent operation.
Square accessible names omit occupants, selection and legal targets.
Enabling reduced motion leaves an existing slide running.
A replacement position retains the prior capture ghost.
Replacing a position leaves delayed capture feedback scheduled.
A parent cannot disable board sounds.
Equivalent parent updates discard a selected piece.
Disabling input leaves the lifted avatar and pointer session alive.
The required Check command waited for nonessential report publication despite completed task verdicts. Watch the lightweight check job rather than the whole Check workflow.

Depot attempt 8zdp3vll5k printed command finished with error, but continuing without the task command, elapsed time or failing stderr. Structured shard diagnostics identify the failure immediately, and the result manifest rejects incomplete or failed checks.

Cold symbolic verification of identity-machine wrote its bound receipt before the models directory existed, causing ENOENT. Create the directory explicitly; independent verifier completion never supplies setup.

The artifact SDK strips URL queries, but Depot redirects encode signed storage credentials inside the proxy pathname, so an SDK info line exposes them. Capture transfer diagnostics in a child process and remove complete URLs before logging.

Parallel TLC verifiers extracted standard modules into shared /tmp/Integers.tla and /tmp/Apalache.tla. A concurrent overwrite produced NullPointerException and module-table lookup failures for the unchanged progress.qnt input. Each checker now owns its JS and JVM temporary directory.

A cold 32-vCPU run observed READY followed by a successful child exit before the PTY delivered DONE. The tty assertion raced process-exit notification and the fixture waited an arbitrary 800ms. Both ends now handshake on exact scroll input and actual READY/DONE output events, retaining all no-echo assertions.

Run b4cx3qcgv1 failed access-sync after emitting only the JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS notice. The checker adapter discarded the child exit signal, leaving the failure undiagnosable. Preserve the signal and include the exact process status in verification errors; the original process failure remains visible and is not retried.

The tooling tests read .depot/workflows/check.yml, package task metadata and specification campaigns, but those files were absent from their cache inputs. The actionlint gate similarly omitted .github/actionlint.yaml. Declare the external configuration these checks actually inspect so changes cannot reuse a stale verdict.

A passing shard could become failed solely because tar packing or actions/upload-artifact failed. The required gate then depended on nonessential evidence. Preserve the validated check verdict; make only the evidence step nonessential. The injected invalid/name artifact failure exercises this separation.
